newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court dismisses Italy's bid for funds under EAGGF.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses Italy's bid for funds under EAGGF.

text.p: The European Court of Justice dismissed on Thursday a plea from the Italian government to require the European Commission to charge more than 67 million dollars to the agricultural guarantee fund.

The Italian government argued the Commission was wrong to deny the funds because they did not apply the EU milk quota scheme in 1991 and to find they did not comply with an obligation to reallocate quantities to qualified producers.

Although court documents say Italy did not challenge that it had not followed the milk quota scheme in a systematic and verifiable manner, it argued that its programme of buying up excess milk quantities had the desired effect of discontinuing the production of milk.

The court rejected that argument and found the restructuring programme set out by the Commission regulation was not designed to reduce the production of milk, but to promote improvement in the production structures of smallholdings.

"In any event, the Italian authorities should have approached the Commission if they considered that the reallociation of the quantities released ran counter to the Community objective of the milk quota scheme," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)
"EAGGF - Clearance of accounts - 1991 - Milk and milk products"
Commission of the European Communities, defendant

application for a partial annulment of Commission decision 94/871/EC of 21 December 1994 on the clearance of the accounts presented by the member states in respect of the expenditure for 1991 of the European Agricultural Guidance and Guarantee Fund (EAGGF), Guarantee Section (OJ 1994 L 352, p. 82)
2. Orders the Italian Republic to pay the costs.
